chunks: The esteemed elder Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Yahya b. Imran al-Ash'ari. He said: Abu Abdillah al-Razi -- and his name is Abdullah b. Ahmad -- narrated to me from Sajjada -- and his name is al-Hasan b. Ali b. Abi Uthman, and the name of Abu Uthman is Habib -- from Muhammad b. Abi Hamza from Mu'awiya b. Wahb from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him).

He said: A wise man sought another wise man for seven hundred parasangs for the sake of seven words. When he caught up with him, he said to him: O you! What is higher than the sky, wider than the earth, richer than the sea, harder than stone, hotter than fire, colder than the bitter cold, and heavier than the stabilizing mountains?

So he said to him: O you! Truth is higher than the sky, justice is wider than the earth, a rich soul is richer than the sea, the heart of a disbeliever is harder than stone, the greedy and possessive is hotter than fire, despair in the mercy of Allah the Mighty and Majestic is colder than the bitter cold, and slander upon the innocent is heavier than the stabilizing mountains.

key_terms.البهتان: False accusation or slander, a grave sin in Islamic ethics
key_terms.الزمهرير: Zamharir -- the extreme bitter cold, sometimes identified with a layer of hell in Islamic eschatology
key_terms.حكيم: A wise man or sage; here used to describe seekers of wisdom in ancient times
key_terms.غنى النفس: The richness/contentment of the soul, an inner spiritual wealth
key_terms.فرسخ: A parasang, an ancient unit of distance approximately equal to 5-6 kilometers

ai.seo_question: What are the seven things greater than the sky, earth, sea, stone, fire, cold, and mountains in Imam al-Sadiq's hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates the wisdom of an ancient sage who traveled seven hundred parasangs to receive seven profound comparisons. Each comparison highlights a spiritual reality that transcends a natural phenomenon -- truth surpasses the heavens, justice the earth, contentment the sea, while the disbeliever's heart, greed, despair of God's mercy, and slander represent the gravest spiritual extremes.
